installer_meta.maintainer_note: Community-maintained (exotic edition). The installer asks for the init system (installer_meta.init_systems, OpenRC first as the default): installer_meta.init_packages names the init and its elogind provider for basestrap/pacstrap, because base alone lets pacman pick dinit's providers and a later openrc then conflicts with them; packages/*.json carry the per-init service packages (openssh-openrc, openssh-dinit, ...) and service names under init.<name>. basestrap is used on an Artix host; anywhere else — the FreedomNAS live ISO included — pacstrap does the same job from pacman, arch-install-scripts and artix-keyring (freedomnas-overlay), pointed at bootstrap_files.pacman_conf with a throwaway keyring and no host mirrorlist (-M). files.pacman_mirrorlist gives the installed system the same mirror. ZFS comes from Chaotic-AUR (repositories.core), as on Arch; its packages ship systemd units only, so the service scripts are built by pkgbuild.install from git: zfs-openrc from the AUR, zfs-dinit from codeberg.org/sarahmeow86/zfs-dinit.

rootpool.create: zpool create -o ashift={ashift} -O acltype=posixacl -O canmount=off -O compression={compression} -O dnodesize=auto -O normalization=formD -O relatime=on -O xattr=sa -O mountpoint=/ -R {altroot} {pool_name} {device}

pacman_conf.content:
[options]
Architecture = auto
SigLevel = Required DatabaseOptional
LocalFileSigLevel = Optional
GPGDir = {bootstrap_dir}/gnupg
ParallelDownloads = 5

[system]
Server = {mirror}/$repo/os/$arch
Server = https://mirrors.dotsrc.org/artix-linux/repos/$repo/os/$arch

[world]
Server = {mirror}/$repo/os/$arch
Server = https://mirrors.dotsrc.org/artix-linux/repos/$repo/os/$arch

[galaxy]
Server = {mirror}/$repo/os/$arch
Server = https://mirrors.dotsrc.org/artix-linux/repos/$repo/os/$arch

install: cd /var/tmp/freedomnas-build/{package_name} && runuser -u freedomnas-build -- env HOME=/var/tmp/freedomnas-build makepkg --nodeps --noconfirm

dracut_uki.content:
# The UKI is built inside a chroot, where dracut's idea of "this host" is
# the installer's, not the machine being installed.
hostonly="no"

fstab.content:
# /etc/fstab - ZFS datasets are mounted by ZFS, not fstab
{esp_spec}	/boot/efi	vfat	defaults	0	2

scheduled_jobs.content:
# FreedomNAS scheduled work. Cron decides when; config.yaml decides what,
# so a system with no policies costs a handful of no-ops a day.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
0  * * * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval hourly  >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
5  0 * * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval daily   >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
10 0 * * 0  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval weekly  >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
15 0 1 * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval monthly >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
# The configuration's shadow copy on every other pool: what a reinstall
# onto a blank disk finds waiting for it on the data pool.
30 3 * * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas shadow-sync                     >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1

sudoers.content:
# FreedomNAS: the WebUI runs updates as the signed-in user,
# and topgrade calls sudo itself for the steps that need root.
%{sudo_group} ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL
